topic: How do interference mitigation techniques adapt when handling tunneled versus non-tunneled traffic in multi-beam satellite systems?
consensus_response: For non-tunneled traffic, array factor's main lobe directivity and sidelobe levels determine interference mitigation effectiveness. With proper array factor design, increased capacity and reduced interference can be achieved. For tunneled traffic, feed weights' amplitude and phase settings affect interference cancellation performance. Hybrid architectures combining beamforming with advanced signal processing techniques provide more efficient interference cancellation and adaptability in dynamic environments.
reference_context: Interference mitigation techniques are crucial for achieving sufficient data rates in multi-beam satellite systems. Non-tunneled traffic is affected by array factor's main lobe directivity and sidelobe levels, while tunneled traffic relies on feed weights' amplitude and phase settings.
